questions.title: How do you invoke a service operation (function import) in OData V2?
questions.description: Service operations expose custom behavior that does not fit the uniform create, read, update and delete interface. A client invokes one by sending an HTTP GET or POST request to its URI; the metadata states the method to use in the HttpMethod attribute of the Function Import. Parameters are simple scalar values of EDM primitive types and are passed in the query string, using the parameter name without a $ prefix and the value in OData literal form, for example GetProductsByRating?rating=4. Servers should allow invocation through GET only when the operation has no side effects. If the operation returns a collection of entries, the service author can enable query composition, so the operation URI can be treated as the starting collection for further URI conventions, such as additional query options.
keyPoints: GET or POST to the operation URI; the method comes from m:HttpMethod.
Parameters: primitive values in the query string, no $ prefix.
GET only for operations without side effects.
Operations returning entries may allow query composition.

examples.title: Calling the function import of the V2 demo service
examples.code:
GET /V2/OData/OData.svc/GetProductsByRating?rating=4 HTTP/1.1
Host: services.odata.org

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/atom+xml;type=feed;charset=utf-8

<feed ...> ...the matching Product entries... </feed>

Wrong HTTP method (the metadata says m:HttpMethod="GET"):
POST /V2/OData/OData.svc/GetProductsByRating?rating=4
-> 405 Method Not Allowed

versionDiff.v2: GET or POST, whichever m:HttpMethod declares.
versionDiff.v4: Functions with GET, actions with POST.
Functions and actions can be bound to a type and called on an instance by appending their qualified name to its URL.
Inline in parentheses after the function name, or as @ parameter aliases; action parameters go in the request body.

questions.title: What can a service operation return, and how is it described in the metadata?
questions.description: A service operation is a function whose semantics are defined by the service author. It accepts primitive input parameters and can be defined to return a single primitive value, a single complex type, a collection of primitives, a collection of complex types, a single entry, a collection of entries, or nothing (void). In the metadata document it is described by a Function Import, which names the operation, lists its parameters, declares its ReturnType and, when it returns entries, the EntitySet they belong to. The V2 demo service has one: GetProductsByRating takes an Edm.Int32 parameter rating and returns Collection(ODataDemo.Product) from the Products entity set. The V2 spec's own examples are ProductsByColor, which returns products, and ProductColors, which takes no parameters and returns a collection of strings.
keyPoints: Returns: primitive(s), complex value(s), an entry, a collection of entries, or void.
Described in $metadata by a Function Import (name, parameters, ReturnType, EntitySet).

examples.title: Function import in the V2 demo service metadata
Other return types, as in the V2 spec examples (not live)
examples.code:
<!-- returns entries -->
<FunctionImport Name="ProductsByColor" ReturnType="Collection(ODataDemo.Product)"
                EntitySet="Products" m:HttpMethod="GET">
  <Parameter Name="color" Type="Edm.String" />
</FunctionImport>

<!-- no parameters, returns a collection of strings -->
<FunctionImport Name="ProductColors" ReturnType="Collection(Edm.String)" m:HttpMethod="GET" />

versionDiff.v2: FunctionImport with ReturnType and m:HttpMethod inside the entity container.
versionDiff.v4: Function or Action element at the schema level with a ReturnType child element; FunctionImport or ActionImport in the container points to it.
The return type can state Nullable.
